newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: Confined to mostly narrow trading ranges, South African stocks ended a touch above overnight closing levels despite a slip in gold shares towards the finish.
Dealers said the market had shown no clear direction on Wednesday, although the underlying sentiment remained positive amid some genuine demand for stock, especially blue-chips later in the day.
"The indi (industrial) 25 index is up much more than the indi 100, which is an indication that there was demand for top blue-chips," one dealer said.
Traders noted good demand for heavyweight Sasol Ltd, both local and offshore, which gave it a strong push up for the second consecutive day to end at 51.25 rand, a gain of 125 cents.
A small number of arbitrage deals, which saw stocks bought in exchange for the sale of related futures contracts, also edged some key shares higher.
Dealers said stocks also received a boost from Wall Street's more than 50-point rise on Tuesday, but jitters on possible inflationary pressures in the United States remained everpresent.
At the close the industrial index was up 5.2 points to 8,249.9 hoisting the all-share index up 4.3 points to 7,048.4.
Dealers said features included Pick 'n Pay which jumped to a new high of 590 cents from 574 after posting year earnings in the top range of analysts' forecasts and predicting further growth.

"We see the company in the next three to five years as being in a fairly strong growth phase, but it has got to be done in a very planned and managed fashion," Pick 'n Pay joint managing director Gareth Ackerman said.
